title: Canonical etale derived adjunction on ordinary chain transposes
statement:
Let $r:W\to V$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $R$ any commutative ring. Work with sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves on small etale sites and the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $r_R^*\dashv r_{*,R}$ for the exact module inverse-image adjunction [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Let $Q$ be localization and let $\alpha_K:Q(r_{*,R}K)\to Rr_{*,R}(QK)$ be the canonical right-derived comparison, defined using K-injective resolutions [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived].

There is a canonical derived adjunction $r_R^*\dashv Rr_{*,R}$, with $r_R^*$ represented termwise [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For any cochain complexes $M$ on $V$ and $K$ on $W$, and any chain map $f:M\to r_{*,R}K$, its Hom bijection satisfies
$$e_R(\alpha_K\circ Qf)=Q(f^\flat),\qquad f^\flat=\varepsilon^0_K\circ r_R^*f:r_R^*M\to K,$$
where the right side uses the canonical exact-pullback identification $r_R^*(QM)\cong Q(r_R^*M)$. The maps $\alpha_K$ and this formula are natural in chain maps in both variables. In particular, setting $M=r_{*,R}K$ and $f=1$ gives
$$\varepsilon_{QK}\circ r_R^*(\alpha_K)=Q(\varepsilon^0_K).$$
No boundedness, acyclicity, flatness or properness assumption is required.

proof.text: Reuse the existing canonical mapDerivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction. Its construction is Adjunction.derived on the homotopy adjunction. Apply Mathlib Adjunction.derivedε_fac_app, as recorded by lem-sc-derived-adjunction-from-underived, with the exact left comparison and the canonical right-derived unit. Use mapHomotopyCategory_counit_app_quotient and mapDerivedCategoryFactorsh_hom_app to express it on complexes. The quotient-to-derived comparison and the homotopy-factor comparison have identity components. Consequently the square is D(L)(alpha_K) followed by the derived counit equals the exact-left comparison followed by Q of the ordinary chain counit. This is chainCounit, a proved private helper.

The inverse Hom equivalence is D(L)(-) followed by the counit. Apply the square from Step 1 to alpha_K, precompose by D(L)(Qf), and use naturality of mapDerivedCategoryFactors and functoriality of Q. This gives the ordinary chain transpose formula. The fourth clause is precisely the square from Step 1. These calculations work for every complex and require no quasi-isomorphism preservation by the right adjoint.

The second clause is the existing rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ_naturality theorem. For the third clause, distribute Q over b followed by f followed by G(k), move the comparison past Q(G(k)) using that theorem, and apply homEquiv_naturality_left_symm and homEquiv_naturality_right_symm. The categorical calculations are packaged in the proved private helper chainTranspose and specialized to the etale adjunction.
